```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 110)
library(cpueTargeting)
library(ggplot2)
# Results: loaded from rdata/ if pre-run (inst/scripts/run_bathymetric.R);
# otherwise computed here if options(cpueTargeting.run_vignettes = TRUE),
# else the code is only shown.
rdata <- getOption("cpueTargeting.rdata", "../rdata")
f_single <- file.path(rdata, "bathymetric_single.rds")
f_reps <- file.path(rdata, "bathymetric_replicates.rds")
preloaded <- file.exists(f_single)
have_single <- preloaded || isTRUE(getOption("cpueTargeting.run_vignettes", FALSE))
have_reps <- file.exists(f_reps)
if (preloaded) {
  x <- readRDS(f_single)
  sim <- x$sim
  fit <- x$fit
}
```

This example uses the spatial multispecies simulator of Thorson et al.
(2017, Appendix A), which generalises the simulator of Ono et al. (2015), with
the "Run 22" settings of the CPUE guidelines. Four species live along
continuous depth-preference gradients over a simulated bathymetry, and 30
vessels move effort between them following species prices, which change in
three 10-year blocks (species 1, then 2, then 4). The simulator is described in
full in the [background document](https://henning-winker.github.io/cpueTargeting/appendix.html).

Positions are reported only as the centres of 5 x 5 blocks. This is the
realistic case: logbooks rarely report positions at the scale at which fish
and fleets interact, so a spatial term cannot resolve all spatial targeting.

# The simulated fishery

The code for the single run (seed 123); all results shown below were pre-run
with `inst/scripts/run_bathymetric.R`:

```{r simulate, eval = FALSE}
sim <- simulate_bathymetric(seed = 123, plots = FALSE)
```

```{r run-live-sim, include = FALSE, eval = have_single && !preloaded, ref.label = "simulate"}
```

```{r om-plots, eval = have_single}
p <- plot_om(sim)
p$Depth
p$SpDens
```

Species 1 and 3 live in patches; species 2 and 4 in the surrounding deeper
water. Catches per set are zero-inflated and right-skewed, so Tweedie GAMs are
used:

```{r hist, eval = have_single}
p$Hist
```

Nominal CPUE (points) against the true biomass (blue): the price-driven
targeting changes bias nominal CPUE by up to a factor of two.

```{r cpue, eval = have_single}
p$CPUE
```

# Standardisation as in the guidelines

All models are Tweedie GAMs with `year` plus a targeting term. `+S` adds a
spatial smoother `s(Xs, Ys, k = 8)` on the 5 x 5 blocks. As in the guidelines,
the catch composition is reduced to two principal components (DPC) and three
clusters (number of PCs + 1). The final DPC model is fitted as a GAMM with a
random vessel effect.

```{r standardise, eval = FALSE}
fit <- standardize_cpue(sim,
  models = c("Base", "Base+S", "Cluster+S", "DPC", "DPC+S"),
  n_pc = 2, n_clusters = 3, spatial_res = 5, spatial_k = 8, engine = "gam")
fit_re <- standardize_cpue(sim, models = "DPC+S",
  n_pc = 2, n_clusters = 3, spatial_res = 5, spatial_k = 8, engine = "gam",
  vessel_re = TRUE, label = " + vessel RE")
fit <- bind_comparisons(fit, fit_re)
```

```{r run-live-fit, include = FALSE, eval = have_single && !preloaded, ref.label = "standardise"}
```

```{r formulas, eval = have_single}
fit$formulas
```

```{r indices, eval = have_single, fig.height = 6}
plot_indices(fit, type = "smooth")
```

```{r rmse, eval = have_single}
plot_diagnostics(fit)
```

* The spatial term on 5 x 5 blocks hardly improves on Base: the habitat
  patches are smaller than the reporting blocks.
* DPC, with or without the spatial term, follows the true trends closely:
  the catch composition carries the fine-scale information that the reported
  positions lack.
* Three discrete clusters capture only part of a continuous gradient.

# What do the PCs capture?

```{r pcs, eval = have_single}
pp <- plot_pcs(fit, pcs = c("PC1", "PC2"))
pp$loadings
pp$space
pp$time
```

PC1 maps the habitat patches at the resolution of single cells, from catches
alone, and jumps when the targeting changes (year 11). PC2 carries little
signal, as in the guidelines, where only PC1 was non-trivial.

# What do the clusters capture?

```{r clusters, eval = have_single}
pc <- plot_clusters(fit, switch_years = c(10.5, 20.5))
pc$composition
pc$time
pc$space
pc$pca
```

The clusters cut the continuous cloud of catch compositions into three
tactics. Their shares change with the targeting, but each cluster mixes sets
from different parts of the gradient.

# Replicates

The same models (without the random vessel effect, and with `engine = "bam"`)
over 20 seeds (`inst/scripts/run_bathymetric.R`):

```{r replicates, eval = have_reps, fig.height = 6}
reps <- readRDS(f_reps)
plot_replicates(reps)
```

Ono, K., Punt, A.E. and Hilborn, R. (2015) Think outside the grids: an
objective approach to define spatial strata for catch and effort analysis.
Fisheries Research 170, 89-101.

Thorson, J.T., Fonner, R., Haltuch, M.A., Ono, K. and Winker, H. (2017)
Accounting for spatiotemporal variation and fisher targeting when estimating
abundance from multispecies fishery data. Canadian Journal of Fisheries and
Aquatic Sciences 74, 1794-1807.

Winker, H., Kerwath, S.E. and Attwood, C.G. (2013) Comparison of two approaches
to standardize catch-per-unit-effort for targeting behaviour in a
multispecies hand-line fishery. Fisheries Research 139, 118-131.

Winker, H., Kerwath, S.E. and Attwood, C.G. (2014) Proof of concept for a novel
procedure to standardize multispecies catch and effort data. Fisheries
Research 155, 149-159.
